name: mudlark
description: Replays how a built artifact came to be, reconstructed from git commits. Captures each commit as a visual snapshot, extracts five layers (Structure, Layout, Surface, Content, Behavior), and plays them back as a continuous, scrubbable film.
author: R. Michael Thomas

one_command.description: Point at any HTML file in a git repo. Mudlark walks up to the repo root, writes an ephemeral subjects/_quick.json, captures every commit, builds the film, and starts the player. Zero config; single state.

capture.description: Snapshot every commit x every declared state. Reads MUDLARK_SUBJECT (falling back to BUILDBACK_SUBJECT) for the subject config name. Default: one-surface.

delta.description: Build per-state deltas and cross-state annotation from existing snapshots, then write the manifest. Reads the same subject env var as capture. Does not launch a browser.

dev.description: Start the Vite dev server for the player. Opens at http://localhost:5173.

verify.description: Record verification: git reader, capture, snapshot hygiene, identity, deltas, pacing, invariants, zero-config, state parity, camera invariance, font determinism. Launches a browser and re-captures.

verify_player.description: Player verification: framing and zoom modes, transport sizing, timeline seek and scrub, keyboard shortcuts, every speed rung, looping and end-of-film. Starts its own dev server.

verify_grammar.description: Grammar verification: asserts the layer order and per-layer property lists in grammar/output.json match src/layers/routing.ts exactly, and that subjects/*.json validate against grammar/subject.schema.json.

typecheck.description: tsc --noEmit over src/, player/, and scripts/.

env.MUDLARK_SUBJECT: Name of the subject config to use, resolved to subjects/<name>.json. Read by capture and delta. Defaults to 'one-surface'.
env.BUILDBACK_SUBJECT: Pre-rename name for the same variable, honored as a fallback when MUDLARK_SUBJECT is unset.

prerequisites.note: Playwright's Chromium is used for headless capture. No other browser is needed.

scope.captures: Anything a browser can render from a static file tree — HTML, SVG, or any page that works by opening the file directly.
scope.does_not_capture: Repos requiring compilation, bundling, or a dev server to render. Build-step support (a 'build adapter') is the primary v2 boundary.
scope.subject_file_note: Any file Chromium can render via file:// or a local HTTP server, not limited to index.html.
also_out_of_scope: Multi-file capture in a single beat

record_rule: Smoothing is permitted in presentation and forbidden in the record. Compress a dead fortnight; do not erase it. Never drop, reorder, or silently merge commits.

source_tree.src/cli.ts: One-command wrapper: resolve repo -> capture -> delta -> serve
source_tree.src/git/: Extract trees at a SHA, read commit metadata
source_tree.src/states/: Declared-state config types and zero-config-safe loader
source_tree.src/capture/: Headless capture: serve -> load -> settle -> state script -> walk -> snapshot
source_tree.src/layers/: Property routing table and per-layer extraction
source_tree.src/pacing/: Named pacing rules over the unaltered commit surface
source_tree.player/: Vite player: DOM reconstruction, interpolation, framing, transport, timeline
source_tree.subjects/: Subject configs, one JSON file per subject
source_tree.grammar/: Machine-readable descriptions of input, output, and project

etymology: The Victorian practice of mudlarking — scavenging the Thames riverbed at low tide for coins, pottery shards, and bones. Mudlark does the same thing with git history.
